reference: util-linux fincore with full raw empty-file tables. Nonempty tables are validated byte-for-byte against independent rendering conditional only on observed PAGES, checked for bounds and RES conversion using independently queried getconf PAGESIZE. Fixed input lengths, SIZE units, headers, spacing and operand order are independently specified. This validates conditional formatting and count bounds, not equality of residency in separate runs.
coverage: Bash type and help metadata for the builtin, checked without invoking fincore operations.
Default table headings and a small nonempty private file.
--noheadings and --bytes aliases on a small file.
Empty-file output, multiple file arguments, and -- option termination for a dash-prefixed relative name.
Missing operand and missing-file failures, including continued output for a valid file beside a missing file.
Human size rounding through 8193 bytes, grouped short options, spaces and repeated filenames, and unknown options.
Nonempty table formatting checked independently of nondeterministic residency; zero-size output compared directly.
exclusions: Cold-page eviction and exact resident-page transitions are deferred until a disposable VM or reviewed mincore shim can control cache state.
No absolute paths, device files, host files, cache eviction, or system-wide operations are exercised.
No cold/warm cache-state claim is inferred from freshly created files.

cases.purpose: Confirm through Bash type metadata that fincore is installed as a builtin.
Confirm the documented fincore help entry is available through Bash help without running a fincore query.
Check every heading and row byte for a private small file, conditional only on its observed PAGES. No resident count is prescribed.
cases.script:
page_size=$(getconf PAGESIZE)
[[ $page_size =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]
# This check asserts table bytes conditional on the observed PAGES value.
# It never requires a page to be resident. Page size is read independently through getconf.
check_table() {
 local heading=$1 bytes=$2 expected_rc=$3 size_width=$4; shift 4
 local table rc line res pages size name i=0 rw=3 pw=5 expected='' row h
 local -a counts=() resident=()
 if table=$(if fincore "$@"; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi; printf '\001'; exit "$rc"); then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
 [[ $rc == "$expected_rc" ]]
 table=${table%$'\001'}
 while IFS= read -r line; do
  if (( heading && i == 0 )); then i=1; continue; fi
  read -r res pages size name <<< "$line"
  [[ $pages =~ ^[0-3]$ ]]
  counts+=("$pages")
 done <<< "${table%$'\n'}"
 [[ ${#counts[@]} == ${#names[@]} ]]
 for ((i=0;i<${#counts[@]};i++)); do
  pages=${counts[i]}
  # Only representation and internal unit conversion are asserted here.
  # The count itself can vary independently in the reference and candidate.
  [[ $pages -le $(( (lengths[i] + page_size - 1) / page_size )) ]]
  if (( bytes )); then
   res=$((pages * page_size))
   if (( pages > 0 )); then rw=5; fi
  else
   resident_bytes=$((pages * page_size))
   if (( resident_bytes < 1024 )); then res=${resident_bytes}B
   else
    printf -v res '%.1f' "$((resident_bytes / 1024))"
    res=${res%.0}K
   fi
   if (( ${#res} >= 3 )); then rw=5; fi
  fi
  resident+=("$res")
 done
 if (( !heading )); then rw=5; pw=1; fi
 if (( heading )); then
  printf -v h '%*s %*s %*s FILE\n' "$rw" RES "$pw" PAGES "$size_width" SIZE
  expected+=$h
 fi
 for ((i=0;i<${#names[@]};i++)); do
  if (( bytes )); then size=${lengths[i]}; else size=${human[i]}; fi
  printf -v row '%*s %*s %*s %s\n' "$rw" "${resident[i]}" "$pw" "${counts[i]}" "$size_width" "$size" "${names[i]}"
  expected+=$row
 done
 if [[ $table != "$expected" ]]; then
  printf 'actual=%q\nexpected=%q\n' "$table" "$expected" >&2
  return 1
 fi
 printf 'validated headings=%s bytes=%s files=%s status=%s\n' "$heading" "$bytes" "${#names[@]}" "$rc"
}
printf 'fincore parity\n' > payload
names=(payload); lengths=(15); human=(15B)
check_table 1 0 0 4 payload

cases.purpose: Exercise exact cold, resident, and page-boundary counts for mincore-based reporting.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r1: Not observable without privilege in the parity VM (probe-fincore-69): mincore(2) reports every page resident for files the caller cannot write (mm/mincore.c can_do_mincore), util-linux fincore cachestat(2) returns EPERM for non-owned files, and every writable scratch area is tmpfs, where POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED evicts nothing. Needs a caller-owned file on a writable non-tmpfs filesystem (root-provisioned ext4 scratch or BLOCK-DEV).; r4: Not observable without privilege in the parity VM (probe-fincore-69): mincore(2) reports every page resident for files the caller cannot write (mm/mincore.c can_do_mincore), util-linux fincore cachestat(2) returns EPERM for non-owned files, and every writable scratch area is tmpfs, where POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED evicts nothing. Needs a caller-owned file on a writable non-tmpfs filesystem (root-provisioned ext4 scratch or BLOCK-DEV).; r5: Not observable without privilege in the parity VM (probe-fincore-69): mincore(2) reports every page resident for files the caller cannot write (mm/mincore.c can_do_mincore), util-linux fincore cachestat(2) returns EPERM for non-owned files, and every writable scratch area is tmpfs, where POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED evicts nothing. Needs a caller-owned file on a writable non-tmpfs filesystem (root-provisioned ext4 scratch or BLOCK-DEV).
